summary: An infringement is unauthorised entry into notified airspace: CAS, prohibited or restricted airspace, active danger areas, ATZ, RMZ or TMZ. Prevent them with pre-flight planning, a correctly configured moving map, a margin of 200 ft vertically or 2 NM horizontally, the right altimeter setting, a UK FIS or a Frequency Monitoring Code. To use an FMC, tune the frequency, check volume, select the code with ALT, listen out, and reset to 7000 afterwards. Built from the Skyway Code pp.12, 89, 133-134.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.12, 89, 133-134
sections: What counts as an infringement
Unauthorised entry into notified airspace: controlled airspace, prohibited or restricted airspace, active danger areas, ATZ, RMZ (radio mandatory zone) and TMZ (transponder mandatory zone)
Can be a serious safety incident and could lead to a mid-air collision
In most infringements pilots were not using a moving map, or not using it correctly
Prevention
Plan the flight in detail, even 'on the dining room table', with a secondary plan
Use a VFR moving map: keep databases up to date, check airspace and NOTAMs, place it where it does not block the lookout and have a backup (draw the route on a 1:500,000 or 1:250,000 chart)
Stay 200 ft below the base of CAS (or over an ATZ, Danger, Prohibited or Restricted area) and 2 NM from the edge of notified airspace. Increase the margin in turbulence
Use the right altimeter setting and note where the base of CAS changes between an altitude and a flight level
Get a UK FIS from an ATSU, or use an FMC
Apply TEM: threats include airspace, NOTAM, weather, distraction and equipment failure. Errors include misidentifying features, not holding altitude and inaccurate headings
Recognise distraction and positively shift attention back to flying
Frequency Monitoring Codes (FMC)
An FMC is selected on the transponder while monitoring an ATC frequency without having established contact
Steps: select the frequency and check volume and reception, select the FMC with ALT (Mode C), listen for your callsign or position, and stay within range of the ATSU
Return to 7000 (VFR) or 2000 (IFR) when you stop monitoring
ATC will endeavour to warn you of a likely infringement but this is not guaranteed and depends on capacity
Each FMC has a published frequency and area (AIP ENR 6-80)
Transponder rules
If you have a serviceable transponder, SERA requires it selected on with altitude reporting at all times
Exceptions: ATC direction or local procedure, airspace where carriage is not required (turn off only to save power)
Switching it off while infringing increases the likely sanction

sum.What counts as an infringement: CAS, restricted airspace, ATZ, RMZ and TMZ.
sum.Prevention: Planning, moving map, 200 ft and 2 NM margins and TEM.
sum.Frequency Monitoring Codes (FMC): Tune, select ALT, listen, then return to 7000.
sum.Transponder rules: Keep it on with ALT unless an exception applies.

quiz.q: A Frequency Monitoring Code is used to:
o: Show you are listening on a frequency without a service
quiz.why: It improves situational awareness for pilot and ATC.

quiz.q: The recommended margin from the base of CAS is:
quiz.why: Plus 2 NM horizontally from the edge of notified airspace.

quiz.q: When leaving the monitored frequency you should:
Which is NOT counted as an infringement?
o: Entering Class G airspace below 1,000 ft
quiz.why: Class G is not notified restricted airspace.

quiz.q: Most infringements occur when the pilot:
o: Did not use or misused a moving map
quiz.why: Moving maps help only when configured and used properly.
